contents.name: Scheme dependence and scale-dependent renormalized coefficients

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete relevant passages in §§2.2.1–2.2.2 and §4.1.3 of the full review, including the Wilson scale cancellation, the physical and MS scheme definitions, and the displayed running equation.

alternatives.argument: On a compact cylinder around the initial point choose finite bounds M and L and a positive h with hM no greater than the state radius and Lh<1. On the complete sup-norm space of continuous curves in the closed state ball, the Volterra operator T(C)(t)=C0+integral from t0 to t of beta(s,C(s)) ds maps the ball to itself and is a contraction with constant at most Lh. Banach gives its unique fixed point, and Volterra equivalence gives a continuously differentiable solution. A first-exit estimate using M shows every solution through the same initial data stays in the ball on the short interval, so it is the same fixed point; local repetition and connectedness give agreement on every common interval. For nearby initial vectors, the solutions lie in a common compact cylinder and satisfy u(d)<=a+L integral_0^d u(s) ds. Repeated substitution gives u(d)<=a sum_{j=0}^{m-1}(Ld)^j/j!+U(Ld)^m/m!, with U bounded by the common cylinder. The remainder tends to zero and the sum tends to exp(Ld), yielding the claimed continuous-dependence estimate. The exact imported theorem, ODE definitions, and integral-equation proposition are declared as dependencies; no global existence or QFT beta calculation is asserted.

source_review.limitations: The result is local. It does not assert global flow, absence of blow-up, perturbative accuracy, or that a QFT beta vector field has been computed.

contents.name: Independent local ODE existence, uniqueness, and common-interval uniqueness proof

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete proof of Lemma 1.5.5, the first-exit argument, Lemma 1.5.9, and the assembly of Theorem 1.5.4 in the full lecture notes.
source_review.supports: The compact-cylinder bounds and local state-Lipschitz constant give a contraction on a closed curve ball; the first-exit estimate extends uniqueness beyond that ball, and a connectedness argument gives uniqueness throughout the common interval.
source_review.limitations: The notes establish ODE well-posedness for the stated mathematical vector field only; they do not identify it with a physical EFT coefficient function or establish global existence.
